title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government’s reply to the 2020 Committee report on AI and Public Standards explains how it will act on the report’s findings, focusing on making AI systems more transparent, safe, and aligned with public values. It outlines a set of policy steps and regulatory measures the government plans to introduce to strengthen accountability, protect privacy, and encourage responsible AI development.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is outlining how it will oversee the use of AI in the qualifications sector, ensuring that any AI tools used in assessments are fair, secure, and reliable. This policy was created after requests from the Secretary of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade, signalling the government’s commitment to responsible AI in education.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how copyright‑protected materials are used to train AI systems, evaluates the legal and economic implications, and offers guidance on balancing innovation with creators' rights. It recommends policy measures and best practices to ensure fair compensation and protect intellectual property while enabling technological progress.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued its reply to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report, “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency”, recognising the committee’s concerns about AI risks and opportunities. It outlines new policies and initiatives to strengthen AI safety, promote ethical development, and keep the country competitive while protecting citizens and the economy.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the scope, objectives, and procedures for a committee tasked with reviewing how AI intersects with public standards, including guidance on stakeholder engagement, evidence gathering, and reporting. It also provides FAQs to clarify the committee’s mandate, roles, and expected outputs for transparency and accountability.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee on how artificial intelligence should be governed. They are offering their perspective to help shape future AI policy decisions.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explores how artificial intelligence is reshaping the rules that govern medical products, aiming to keep them safe, effective, and ethical. It proposes ways to update existing regulations and apply the AI White Paper principles to the approval and ongoing oversight of medical devices.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organisation the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential defence force for its size by using AI. It focuses on harnessing AI to strengthen operations, improve decision‑making, and keep the organisation at the forefront of defence technology.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: This plan outlines how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to harness AI benefits and mitigate risks. It focuses on maximizing opportunities while addressing safety, privacy, and ethical concerns.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report examines how copyright‑protected materials are being used in AI development. It evaluates progress and challenges under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
